If your main need is “help me clearly explain what my business does online”, I’d compare agencies across three buckets: brand/messaging, website, and local customer acquisition. Toronto has strong options in each. 
Clutch
+1

My shortlist

Brand Vision Marketing - Web Design & Branding — best all-around starting point. Combines brand strategy, visual identity, web design and SEO, so you can get the message and website aligned rather than hiring separate firms. Clutch currently lists it at 5.0 with 65 reviews. 
Clutch

Whissel Strategies - Toronto Marketing Agency — good for a small business wanting ongoing marketing help. Its positioning is particularly focused on customer acquisition and end-to-end marketing execution.

Web Sharx — good website + branding option. Especially worth comparing if you need someone to turn your offering into a clear, professional site while also handling design and digital marketing.

Page Pros — worth a look if local search matters. It specializes in local SEO/digital marketing, which can be important for a Toronto storefront or service-area business.

ThrillX Design - Web Design Company Toronto — good if conversion is the priority. Its focus is conversion-oriented websites, UX and messaging rather than simply making a site look attractive.

Goods & Services Branding — best comparison if your real challenge is positioning. It combines research, strategy, messaging, identity and digital implementation rather than treating branding as just a logo.

Third Eye Insights | Brand Strategy Toronto — interesting boutique option for founder-led businesses. Its emphasis is on positioning, differentiation and messaging.

For a newly opened local business, I'd probably get proposals from Brand Vision + Whissel Strategies + Page Pros, then add Goods & Services if you're still unsure how to articulate the business itself.

What to ask each agency

Give all of them the same brief and ask them to explain:

Who they think your ideal Toronto customer is.

How they'd describe your business in one sentence.

What makes you different from competitors.

What the homepage should communicate in the first 5–10 seconds.

How they'll generate local discovery — Google/Maps, SEO, social, paid ads, etc.

What they'll actually deliver in the first 90 days.

Total setup cost and ongoing monthly cost.

How success will be measured: calls, bookings, store visits, leads, sales, or something else.

Don't choose based on the prettiest portfolio alone. For a local business, clear positioning + a strong website + local search visibility is usually a much more useful combination than an expensive “branding” exercise.

If you tell me what kind of local business you're opening and roughly what you want to spend (e.g. <$5k, $5–15k, $15k+), I can narrow this to 3 Toronto agencies that are the best fit and compare their likely strengths/pricing.
